title: Smooth coordinate chart after dividing normal coordinates by a uniformizer
statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Let $r,n\geq0$ and let $C$ be an etale $R[y_1,\ldots,y_r,z_1,\ldots,z_n]$-algebra: the induced affine-scheme morphism is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Use the same letters for the coordinate images in $C$. Put $J=(\pi,z_1,\ldots,z_n)$ and let $C[J/\pi]\subseteq C[1/\pi]$ be the $C$-subalgebra generated by $b/\pi$ for $b\in J$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. The map
$$C[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(\pi t_1-z_1,\ldots,\pi t_n-z_n)\longrightarrow C[J/\pi],\qquad t_j\longmapsto z_j/\pi$$
is an isomorphism. Write $C'$ for this algebra and $z'_j=z_j/\pi$. The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}C'\to\operatorname{Spec}R[y_1,\ldots,y_r,z'_1,\ldots,z'_n]$ is etale. In particular $C'$ is smooth and flat over $R$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-flat-morphism], is Noetherian (every ideal is finitely generated), and $C'[1/\pi]=C[1/\pi]$. Its differential module [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] is free with basis $dy_1,\ldots,dy_r,dz'_1,\ldots,dz'_n$; the canonical differential map sends $dy_i$ to $dy_i$ and $dz_j$ to $\pi\,dz'_j$.

source.place: BLR 3.2 Proposition 3 and 3.3 Proposition 5 proof, printed pp.64 and 70 (PDF pages 70 and 76): ambient dilatation and its differential basis. Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf.

proof.text: Put $P=R[y_1,\ldots,y_r,z_1,\ldots,z_n]$ and $Q=R[y_1,\ldots,y_r,t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, with $P\to Q$ fixing $R,y_i$ and sending $z_j\mapsto\pi t_j$. Set $B=C[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(\pi t_j-z_j:1\le j\le n)$. There is an explicit $Q$-algebra isomorphism $Q\otimes_P C\cong B$: send $q\otimes c$ to $q(y,t)c$, which is balanced because $z_j=\pi t_j$ in $B$. Conversely send $c\in C$ to $1\otimes c$ and $t_j$ to $t_j\otimes1$. The relations vanish by balancing over $P$, and the two composites fix all generators, hence are identities. These assertions use only evaluation in polynomial rings and the tensor-product universal property.

source.place: Lemma 00U2 (lemma-etale), base-change construction, with the explicit presentation substitution $z_j=\pi t_j$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change] to the given etale affine map $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}P$ and $P\to Q$. Step 1 identifies its base change with $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}Q$, so this map is etale. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine] the ring map $Q\to B$ is etale. The polynomial ring $Q$ has $r+n$ variables over $R$; [lem-weil-pbc-etale-polynomial-standard-smooth] therefore makes $B$ standard smooth over $R$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-is-smooth] and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat] to obtain that $R\to B$ is smooth and that $B$ is a flat $R$-module. This flatness will remove the possible extra uniformizer torsion in a general blowup-chart presentation.

source.place: 3.2 Proposition 3 proof, printed p.64 (PDF p.70); algebraic inputs Stacks 00U2 (lemma-etale), 02GJ (lemma-etale-characterize), 00T7 (lemma-standard-smooth).

proof.text: The DVR $R$ is a domain and its uniformizer $\pi$ is nonzero: otherwise its nonzero maximal ideal $\pi R$ would vanish. By [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain], multiplication by every power of $\pi$ on $B$ is injective. The fraction equality in [def-weil-ring-localization-away] now shows $B\to B[1/\pi]$ is injective. Explicit mutually inverse maps identify $B[1/\pi]$ with $C[1/\pi]$: the map to $C[1/\pi]$ fixes $C$ and sends $t_j$ to $z_j/\pi$, while the reverse map is induced by $C\to B[1/\pi]$; the relations give $t_j=z_j/\pi$, so both composites fix the generators and $1/\pi$. The image of $B$ is thus $C[z_1/\pi,\ldots,z_n/\pi]$. Every $b\in J$ can be written $b=\pi c_0+\sum_j z_jc_j$, so $b/\pi=c_0+\sum_j c_j(z_j/\pi)$; conversely each $z_j/\pi$ is an allowed generator. Hence the image is exactly $C[J/\pi]$, proving the asserted isomorphism and $C\xrightarrow{} C\!\left[J/\pi\right]\subseteq C[1/\pi]$. In particular $C'[1/\pi]=C[1/\pi]$.

source.place: 3.2 affine construction, printed pp.62–64 (PDF pp.68–70): the general chart quotient by uniformizer torsion; here flatness proves this torsion zero.

proof.text: Identify $B=C'$ and $t_j=z_j/\pi=z\prime_j$. The $Q$-structure from step 2 is exactly the coordinate map in the statement (the target polynomial ring denotes the abstract polynomial algebra with these named generators). Thus the asserted affine morphism is etale. The smooth ring map $R\to C'$ from step 2 gives a smooth morphism $\operatorname{Spec}C'\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine]; [lem-pc-smooth-flat] makes this morphism flat. Noetherianity requires no additional finiteness assumption: each ideal of the DVR $R$ is principal, hence finitely generated. Smoothness in [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] includes finite presentation, so $C'$ is a quotient of a polynomial ring in finitely many variables over $R$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] directly to $R\to C'$ to conclude that $C'$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Lemma 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), Definition 00T2 (definition-smooth); Morphisms 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize), 01V7 (lemma-smooth-syntomic); More on Morphisms 02H6.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine] for both $P\to C$ and $Q\to C\prime$. It supplies exactly the zero relative differentials and zero first cotangent homology required by [lem-trf-formally-etale-differentials-base-change]. The latter identifies $C\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}\cong\Omega_{C/R}$ and $C\prime\otimes_Q\Omega_{Q/R}\cong\Omega_{C\prime/R}$, sending $c\otimes dx$ to $c\,dx$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis], these give the respective bases $(dy_i,dz_j)$ and $(dy_i,dt_j)$. To see explicitly that extension of the polynomial basis remains a basis, tensor its coordinate isomorphism $\Omega_{Q/R}\cong Q^{r+n}$ with $C\prime$ and use $C\prime\otimes_Q Q^{r+n}\cong(C\prime)^{r+n}$, whose inverse sends a tuple $(c_a)$ to $\sum_a c_a\otimes e_a$. Hence the latter basis is exactly $(dy_i,dz\prime_j)$, including the case of no variables.

source.place: Lemma 0H93 (lemma-formally-etale-omega), final assertion; Lemma 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring). BLR 3.3 Proposition 5 proof, printed p.70 (PDF p.76).

proof.text: For completeness the canonical map is the $C\prime$-linear map $C\prime\otimes_C\Omega_{C/R}\to\Omega_{C\prime/R}$ sending $c\prime\otimes dc$ to $c\prime\,d(c|_{C\prime})$. Indeed composition of $C\to C\prime$ with the universal $R$-derivation is an $R$-derivation, so the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] gives this map. It sends $1\otimes dy_i$ to $dy_i$. Since $z_j=\pi z\prime_j$ and $d\pi=0$ for relative differentials over $R$, the Leibniz rule gives $d z_j=d(\pi z\prime_j)=\pi\,dz\prime_j+z\prime_j\,d\pi=\pi\,dz\prime_j$. This proves the stated formula with its canonical map, rather than just an abstract identification of free modules.

source.place: Definition 07BK (definition-differentials), Lemma 00RO (lemma-universal-omega); BLR 3.3 Proposition 5 proof, printed p.70 (PDF p.76).

The statement is unchanged from the imported one, there are no new nodes and this is a first delivery, not a re-split. The six steps check out. (1) The tensor presentation Q⊗_P C ≅ B = C[t]/(πt−z) is written out with its balancing step. (2) Stacks 00U2 base change plus the étale ring-map/affine equivalence make Q→B étale; etale-polynomial-standard-smooth (r+n variables) then gives B standard smooth, smooth and flat over R. (3) The DVR is a domain with π≠0, so lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain makes B π-torsion-free; that gives B ↪ B[1/π] = C[1/π] with image C[z/π] = C[J/π], and both inclusions are checked through b = πc0 + Σ z_j c_j. (4) Étale, smooth and flat over R and Noetherian (a DVR is a principal ideal ring; Stacks 00FN). (5) Ω=0 and H1=0 from the étale ring-map node are exactly the hypotheses of the 0H93 leaf, so Ω_{C'/R} = C'⊗Ω_{Q/R} is free on dy, dz'. (6) The canonical map gives dz_j = π dz'_j by the Leibniz rule and dπ=0. Edge cases n=0, r=n=0, π a unit in C, and C=0 are all consistent with the statement and proof.
